title: Condon's tempos when drinking
summary: When Ed drank he would take fast tunes slow and slow ones fast and the band followed whatever he started.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Now, another thing you hear of musicians and different ones talking -- some people say Condon had a terrific timing; other people say he didn't have. What was this? He always used---

Well, Ed drank a lot you know and if Ed was drinking, he would have a habit of doing such strange things like now - you say you play a song -- when I was up there, we had set tempos for everything we did; a fast song was a fast song and sometimes Ed would come up and play the fast ones slow and the slow ones fast. And, it would throw you a loop sometimes.
Well, play it - of course. Whichever way he'd beat it off that's the way we'd play it.
That's the way you played it.
Yes. But, sometimes the fast one
would sound pretty awful slow and then a slow one would sound pretty awful fast.
You didn't try to change the time as youstarted off and then go into the right tempo-
No, no. But, when Ed was altogether and had his senses and everything, he knew what to do. He knew how to do it.
Does it help a jazz band like that to have a good guitar player in it; I mean, he was there half the time and half the time he wasn't there.
Well, I just got through telling you that it didn't make any difference whether he was up there or not because out front, I don't think they heard him.
Well, it didn't make that much difference to the band because we had a hell of a rhythm section and Ed could always play in time but you never did--- actually, you didn't hear him very good.
